name: application-swipeable-card-carousel
title: Swipeable Card Carousel
description: A snap-scrolling horizontal row of product cards with an edge peek and dot pagination, driven by touch/scroll rather than arrow buttons.
useWhen: Showing a browsable row of multiple items (products, articles) where users swipe or scroll horizontally, with the next card peeking at the edge as an affordance.
A touch-first mobile or tablet layout where native scroll-snap gestures are preferable to explicit prev/next controls.
avoidWhen: Displaying a single full-width hero image/slide at a time with explicit prev/next arrows and slide indicators — `Carousel`'s single-slide layout fits that shape better.
The item count is small enough (2-3) to just lay out in a static row without scrolling.
responsiveBehavior: Cards are sized as a percentage of the scroll container width so roughly 1.3 cards are visible at once at any viewport, preserving the peek affordance; the row scrolls horizontally with CSS scroll-snap.
accessibility: The scroll container is native-scrollable and keyboard-reachable via standard horizontal scroll/arrow-key behavior, unlike carousels that trap focus in JS-only controls.
Card content (title, description, price) is plain text within each card, readable independent of scroll position.
Dot pagination indicators use an elongated shape for the current position, distinguishing it by shape and size, not color alone.

variants.title: Recommended products
variants.description: A 'Recommended for you' row of four product cards (image, title, subtitle, price) in a snap-scrolling container with a partially visible peeking card and dot pagination beneath.
accessibility: The row uses native horizontal scroll-snap, reachable via touch, mouse drag, or keyboard scroll.

variants.title: Recommended products (Dark)
variants.description: Swipeable card carousel adapted for dark surfaces, including card borders, gradient thumbnails, and pagination dots.
accessibility: Card titles, subtitles, and prices all meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark card background.
